question: On what grounds does the potter and clay example establish an agent relation for the case referred to by 'this'?
premises: Clay and jar and so forth are produced by a potter.
The relation is one of agent to material/product.
That relation is offered as a comparison for another case.
inference: Just as a potter acts on clay for products, so too the case referred to stands in an agent relation.
uncertainties: The precise tertium comparationis is to be limited to agency, not to material identity.
plain_english: As clay, jar, and so forth are made by a potter, so indeed is this.
